message.content:
For a garden sculpture you’ll want a stone that balances **workability** (so you can carve the details you want) with **durability** (so it withstands weather, wind, and occasional foot traffic). | Stone | Why it’s popular for garden sculptures | |-------|----------------------------------------| | **Marble** | • Soft enough to carve fine detail.
• Classic look, available in many colors (white, gray, pink, green).
• Holds patina over time, giving a subtle aging effect. | | **Granite** | • Extremely hard and weather‑resistant – ideal for outdoor settings.
• Less detail than marble, but great for bold, geometric forms.
• Comes in a wide range of colors and textures. | | **Limestone** | • Softer than granite, easier to carve than marble.
• Good for a natural, earthy look.
• Can weather to a soft gray or develop a mossy patina. | | **Sandstone** | • Very workable, excellent for detailed carving.
• Weathering can create a rustic, weathered appearance.
• Not as durable as granite, but still suitable for sheltered garden spots. | **Bottom line:** - If you want a classic, highly detailed piece that ages gracefully, **marble** is the go‑to choice. - If you need maximum durability and can accept a more rugged aesthetic, **granite** is the best bet. Both stones are widely used in garden sculpture, so choose based on the style you’re aiming for and how exposed the piece will be to the elements.
